articles.title: Can Nepal protect Yomari?
articles.summary: The article examines why Nepal lacks a legal framework to safeguard Yomari, a beloved Newari sweet that symbolizes the nation’s intangible cultural heritage. It outlines the gaps in existing heritage laws, the absence of specific protection for traditional foods, and the challenges of recognizing such items under UNESCO conventions. Experts and community leaders argue that legislation, documentation, and public awareness are needed to prevent commercial exploitation and cultural erosion. The piece calls for coordinated action among the Ministry of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation, local cultural bodies, and policymakers to establish protective measures that honor Nepal’s culinary legacy.

articles.title: Ronaldo, Chitwan’s famed wild elephant, found dead
articles.summary: Ronaldo, a celebrated wild bull elephant in Chitwan, Nepal, was found dead. The animal was a crucial breeding partner for captive female elephants, having sired 38 calves. His death raises concerns for local elephant conservation and breeding programs.

articles.title: Nepal leaders call for stronger governance, inclusion on Constitution Day
articles.summary: Nepal's leaders emphasized the importance of stronger governance and inclusion on Constitution Day, stressing social justice and constitutional implementation.

articles.title: Women’s struggles, social movements brought together in new book
articles.summary: The newly released book 'Shared Dreams Woven by Struggle' chronicles the lives of 13 Nepali women leaders who have championed rights, dignity, and social justice. Through personal narratives and historical context, the volume highlights the challenges these women faced and the collective movements that emerged from their struggles, underscoring the ongoing fight for gender equality in Nepal.

articles.title: Trump says he is banning media outlets CNN, MS NOW, Politico from White House
articles.summary: President Donald Trump announced plans to bar several media outlets—including CNN, MSNBC (referred to as MS NOW) and Politico—from White House premises, accusing them of spreading "fake news." The move has sparked fresh concerns over First Amendment rights and press freedom, drawing criticism from journalists and civil‑liberties groups.

articles.title: Nepal begins probe into what triggered Bhotekoshi disaster
articles.summary: The Nepalese government has formed a seven‑member expert panel to investigate the causes of the Bhotekoshi disaster that occurred on August 26. The panel will examine the event from its origin to downstream impacts, assessing geological, glacial and hydrological hazards and exploring any contribution from climate change. The investigation aims to identify triggers and improve future disaster risk management.

articles.title: Princess Diana through her brother’s eyes
articles.summary: British author Charles Spencer, Princess Diana’s brother, is set to release a new memoir that revisits Diana’s life and legacy ahead of the 30th anniversary of her death. The book promises personal insights, family anecdotes, and reflections on Diana’s impact on the royal family and the public. Spencer aims to portray his sister beyond the media’s portrayal, highlighting her humanitarian work and personal struggles. The memoir arrives at a time when interest in Diana’s story remains strong, offering readers a fresh perspective from someone who knew her intimately.

articles.title: Defending the constitution, changing it too
articles.summary: On Constitution Day, Nepal marked the adoption of the 2015 charter with official ceremonies and speeches praising its role in ending monarchy and establishing federalism. However, journalists and civil‑society leaders highlighted that the same document leaves many groups—particularly Madhesis, Dalits, women and other minorities—still facing exclusion from political representation, land rights and public services. Critics argued that while the constitution enshrines fundamental rights, its implementation mechanisms are weak and the federal boundaries favour dominant groups. The government pledged to address these gaps through amendments and inclusive policies, but opposition parties warned that without genuine power‑sharing the promise of a unified, democratic Nepal remains unfulfilled.

articles.title: Mud and steep cliffs hamper efforts to reopen flood-hit roads
articles.summary: More than three weeks after the Bhotekoshi River floods, heavy mud and steep cliffs continue to block road repairs in central Nepal. The districts of Rasuwa and Nuwakot remain isolated from each other, and the headquarters of Dhading district still lacks a direct road connection. Authorities are struggling to clear debris and stabilize slopes, delaying the reopening of critical transport links that are essential for relief supplies and local economies.

articles.title: Greenland, Denmark say US deal will not cede sovereignty
articles.summary: Greenland and Denmark have clarified that a recently announced agreement with the United States will not transfer sovereignty over the self‑governed Danish territory. Details of the deal, including the extent of U.S. military presence and any potential influence on Greenland's foreign policy or resource management, remain undisclosed.

articles.title: Why Constitution Day is still Madhesh’s ‘Black Day’
articles.summary: The 2015 Constitution of Nepal is still seen as a 'Black Day' by the Madheshi people due to policy choices that limited their political representation and access to civil service.

articles.title: Man Kumar and Ram Maya win at Vietnam Mountain Marathon
articles.summary: Man Kumar Roka Magar secured first place in the 100km race and Ram Maya Budha won the 50km category at the Vietnam Mountain Marathon, an event that forms part of the World Trail Majors series, highlighting Nepal's strength in ultra‑distance trail running.

articles.title: Nepali MMA star Yuki Angdembe beats China’s Buhuogubu in JCK-123
articles.summary: In the JCK-123 event held in Luliang, Nepali mixed martial arts star Yuki Angdembe secured his ninth professional win by defeating China's Buhuogubu. Angdembe dominated the bout with superior grappling and wrestling control, sweeping all three judges' scorecards.

articles.title: Wagle to tour US, Doha and Bangkok seeking help after climate-triggered Rasuwa floods
articles.summary: Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Janak Raj Wagle will travel to the United States, Doha and Bangkok to solicit international assistance for the recovery from the climate‑triggered floods that devastated Rasuwa district. The mission aims to secure financial aid, technical expertise and humanitarian support. Prime Minister Balendra Shah is also set to raise the issue of climate justice at the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York, urging global cooperation on climate‑related disasters affecting Nepal.

articles.title: Fees keep Nepal-Israel farm, care worker deals on hold
articles.summary: Negotiations on Nepal‑Israel agreements to send Nepali farm and care workers to Israel have stalled because of a dispute over recruitment fees. Israeli authorities argue that private recruitment agencies have the legal right to charge workers for placement, while the Nepali government insists that recruitment should be free or at least worker‑friendly, warning that high fees exploit migrants. The deadlock threatens to delay the deployment of thousands of Nepali workers seeking higher wages abroad and raises concerns about labor rights, remittances, and bilateral ties.

articles.title: Constitution Day puts Nepal’s constitutional future in focus
articles.summary: On Constitution Day, Nepal's political leaders praised the achievements of the 2015 constitution but diverged on the next steps. The ruling coalition argues that full implementation of existing provisions should be the priority, while opposition parties call for a comprehensive review and possible amendments to address lingering gaps. Debates focus on issues such as federal restructuring, minority rights, and the balance of power between the executive and legislature. The discourse highlights both consensus on the charter's core values and deep divisions over how to adapt it to evolving political realities, underscoring the constitutional future as a central theme in Nepal's governance agenda.

articles.title: Constitution review mired in political debate as parties fail to agree on scope of amendment
articles.summary: The Kathmandu Post reports that the constitutional review process in Nepal has stalled due to intense political disagreement. The Balendra Shah-led government formed a panel to draft proposed amendments, but key political parties have not endorsed the panel's mandate or the scope of changes. The lack of consensus has turned the review into a contentious debate, raising doubts about the timeline and feasibility of any constitutional reform.

articles.title: Can ‘Mission 2026’ finally deliver Nepal its first Asian Games gold?
articles.summary: After three years of preparation hindered by funding challenges, Nepal's streamlined team of 135 athletes has arrived at the Asian Games with the goal of securing double‑digit medals and, for the first time, a gold medal. The initiative, dubbed “Mission 2026,” aims to elevate Nepal’s sporting performance on the continental stage and bring national pride. While financial constraints have limited resources, the contingent remains optimistic about achieving historic success.

articles.title: Lumbini Lions to face Sudurpaschim Royals in NPL opener
articles.summary: Reigning champions Lumbini Lions will begin their title defence in the Nepal Premier League (NPL) against Sudurpaschim Royals at Kirtipur. The opening match starts a 27‑day schedule that includes 21 league fixtures and four playoff games.

articles.title: Fiction: The making of a revolution
articles.summary: The fictional piece titled “The making of a revolution” portrays a society spiraling into chaos after a brutal crackdown on dissent. As the movement gains momentum, widespread anger, personal ambition, and political opportunism drive the narrative forward, illustrating how a once‑unified cause fragments under pressure. The story follows the rise of Deshbhumi, a region caught between the desire for change and the destabilising forces that threaten to undermine it, highlighting the volatile interplay of power, fear, and hope in a revolutionary context.

articles.title: Ed Sheeran says he made ‘mistakes’ amid Macklemore controversy
articles.summary: British singer Ed Sheeran admitted he made "mistakes" after becoming entangled in a controversy sparked by rapper Macklemore's comments on free speech and the Israel‑Palestine conflict. Sheeran said the debate was political and far beyond the music scene, and he did not intend to take a side. He expressed regret for any misunderstanding and clarified his stance, emphasizing that he prefers to stay out of political disputes.

articles.title: Flames, smoke seen near Riyadh airport; Houthis claim attacks on Saudi capital
articles.summary: Flames and smoke were observed near Riyadh airport as the Houthis claimed to have launched an attack on Saudi Arabia's capital. The incident occurred amid a recent surge in Houthi strikes against Saudi targets. Riyadh authorities warned residents of potential aerial threats, and Saudi air defenses reported intercepting a missile aimed at the city.

articles.title: Nepal’s Sanu Maya Thing knocked out in Asian Games karate
articles.summary: Two Nepalese athletes were eliminated in the opening stages of the Asian Games. Karateka Sanu Maya Thing was knocked out of her event, and wushu competitor Vijay Singhjali also lost in his first round. The early exits highlight challenges faced by Nepal's contingent at the multi‑sport event.

articles.title: Udayapur Hospital gets services moving again
articles.summary: Udayapur Hospital in Nepal, after years of unreliable service, is restoring key medical units to full operation. The hospital is addressing chronic staffing shortages and financial constraints to improve patient care and service continuity. While the revival of services marks a positive step for the community, ongoing challenges remain as administrators work to secure sustainable funding and recruit qualified personnel.

articles.title: Heavy rain threat looms from Thursday
articles.summary: Meteorological agencies warn that weather systems forming over the Andaman Sea and the Bay of Bengal could trigger prolonged heavy rain across Nepal from September 24 to 28. The western and central regions are expected to receive the most intense downpours, raising concerns about flooding and landslides. Residents are advised to stay alert and prepare for possible disruptions.
